Olga / Aditya — notes from infra POV:

- For 25 req/s steady with 60 req/s peak, assuming 1.2k token avg response and KV caching for repeated prefixes, expect 18–22ms token latency and sustained throughput on a 4-GPU dedicated pool using our Optimizer runtime.
- Batching: enable adaptive batching with a 30ms batching window; that yields ~2–3x effective throughput improvement without materially impacting median latency.
- Cost delta: Q8 (dynamic 8-bit) gives ~35% cost reduction vs FP16 runtime; Q4 gives ~55% but risk of subtle quality drift on abstractive summarization.

Recommendation for pilot pricing: publish two SKU lines in the sheet — one for baseline (FP16 + caching) and one for Q8. Offer Option B as a $18k commit for the 90 days with a $4.5k pilot credit applied up front (25% effective). Keep Q4 as an advisory path post-validation, not in the initial pilot SKU.

Samir, quick technical addendum for the pilot run and validation plan:

- Data routing: route 20% of traffic to Q8 variant and 80% to FP16 for the first 10 days; capture sample outputs and run automated ROUGE/BERTScore checks + a small human pass on 200 examples.
- KV cache config: TTL=300s for session reuse, cache warmup batch of 500 recent prefixes. This minimizes cold-start token spend while preserving freshness.
- Fallbacks: automatic model fallback to FP16 if quality regression >2% on eval metric; we can wire this into Redwood Console for an easy rollback.

I'll also prepare a short sample evaluation harness we can run against your prompt set — should take 3 business days to execute after we get the sample data.
